atoms.text: Rhys wants to show you around the cities in Wales. Will you visit some cities with him?

instruction.text: Rhys wants to know if you recognise what Welsh towns and cities look like. Select the images of towns and cities in Wales.

feedback.end: Over half of the Welsh population live near the sea in cities such as Cardiff and Swansea. Other people are very spread out across the country.
feedback.wrong: This is New York in the USA. Welsh cities don’t have skyscrapers.

instruction.text: Rhys asks if you know what you might find in Welsh towns and cities. Drag the images to the correct words.
Rhys has marked a few of Wales’ biggest cities on his map. Find Swansea on the map to visit it.
instruction.sound: Rhys has marked a few of Wales’s biggest cities on his map. Find Swansea on the map to visit it.

instruction.text: This is Swansea. Find the boats in the image to learn more.

feedback.end: Swansea is the second biggest city in Wales after Cardiff. It used to be a tiny town, but it grew very quickly in the 19th century.

instruction.text: Find Newport on the map to visit it.
This is Newport. Find the bridges in the image to learn more.

feedback.end: Newport has been a port since the medieval times. It was historically a very important place in Wales for trading coal.

instruction.text: Find Bangor on the map to visit it.
This is Bangor. Find the pier in the image to learn more.
instruction.sound: This is Banggor. Find the pier in the image to learn more.

end.text: Bangor is the very oldest city in Wales and one of the smallest cities in the whole of the UK.
